Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Amar Bahadur Maurya, learned counsel for the applicant and Ms. Munna Mishra,
learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri S.P. Pandey, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 268 of 2024, under Sections 452, 363, 366, 376, 506 of IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Bhamora, District - Bareilly, during the pendency of trial.

PROSECUTION STORY:
3. The applicant is stated to have taken the sister of the victim on a trip and had gang raped her along with co-accused Arpit @ Anshul on 20.05.2024.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:

sentences.text: The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
5. The FIR is delayed by more than two months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. The statement of the victim was recorded u/s 183 of B.N.S.S. wherein she has stated that it was the applicant who raped her and other persons were standing outside the room.
The said story has undertaken a sea change.
The allegations against him are false.
7. The victim by her physical appearance seems to be major although she is marginally less than 17 years as per her school certificate.
8. There is medical evidence to support the prosecution story.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

10. The applicant is languishing in jail since 31.07.2024, having no criminal history to his credit,
deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/ STATE:
11.
The bail application has been opposed on the ground that the date of birth of the victim was 02.06.2007, as such, she comes out to be 16 years 11 months and 22 days.
The consent of minor, if any, cannot be taken into consideration.
However, the other submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

CONCLUSION:
12. The date of birth of the victim as per school certificate is 02.06.2007, as such, she may be considered major in light of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673, wherein it has been opined that it is more often in the Indian Society that person shows the age of their wards much below than their actual age.
13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

14. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the Akash vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99777391/
2 procedure must be just and reasonable.

sentences.text:
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
15.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view, the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595, has again emphasized that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
16. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Akash, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 351 BNSS.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
